chapter: Solo years, marriages and the Canadian party
title: Working without Buck
summary: Life stayed the same but he had to rehearse his own music and depend on himself on stage; he did not seek a new partner.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: It's not that important if you don't remember his name. The important thing is how your life changed without Buck.

Well, life didn't change, the situations changed. Life stayed the same, you know. But the situation to do things was different. See I had to rehearse my own music where he used to rehearse. I had to depend on myself instead of depending on him as a person I want to talk to on the stage. Had to talk to myself before I went on and after I come off. So I had nothing to go to but myself.
Did you consider getting another partner?
No, not yet. I didn't think it was the thing to do.
What about traveling by yourself. Did people very often feel that it wasn't Buck and Bubbles? Did you feel that the public was missing a partner for

Naw, they figured it, if they saw Buck and Bubbles, they can miss Buck. If they saw our act they could miss him, but they could look at me and find out they missed him, only look at me and say, wonder how he feels without his partner. Because I was busy from the time I hit the stage until I went off but you couldn't tell who was supposed to be with me. If there was a lull and for some reason he wasn't there, it would be different. But it wasn't, which was something to think about.
